q: The legal principle by which the Clearing Corporation becomes the central counterparty to all trades is called:
e: Novation is the substitution of a new party (the Clearing Corp) into a contract, replacing the original counterparties' bilateral exposure with exposure to the CC.

q: The minimum net worth required for a Clearing Member who clears trades for other TMs is:
e: ₹3 crore (₹300 lakh) for a CM who clears for other TMs. ₹1 crore for self-only. Plus ₹50 lakh deposit + ₹10 lakh per additional TM cleared.

q: Since October 2019, all open positions in stock futures and stock options on expiry are settled by:
e: Stock derivatives switched to mandatory physical delivery on expiry from October 2019. Index F&O continues to be cash-settled.

q: Interoperability of clearing corporations was implemented in India in:
e: Interoperability was implemented in 2019 (proposed in 2018). Brokers can now clear and settle trades from any exchange through their preferred clearing corporation.

o: Before market open the next day
e: MTM cash settlement happens before market open on T+1, debiting/crediting clearing members' accounts at designated clearing banks.

q: The Investor Protection Fund (IPF) compensates client claims up to:
e: IPF caps payout at ₹25 lakh per client per default. Different from SGF, which is a system-level pool covering CM defaults.

q: In the default cascade, the FIRST resource used is:
e: Cascade: Defaulting member's margins/collateral → SGF → CC own capital → Surviving member contributions. Always defaulter pays first.

q: Initial margin in derivatives is computed using which methodology?
e: SPAN (Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk) computes margin across 16 hypothetical price + volatility scenarios; covers ~99% confidence loss over a one-day horizon.

q: If a client has a long position in 10 lots of SBI futures on NSE and a short position in 6 lots on BSE, with interoperability enabled, the margin will be calculated for:
o: No margin since they offset perfectly
e: With interoperability, positions in the same contract across exchanges are netted at a single clearing corp. Net position = 4 lots long → margin computed on this netted position.

q: Liquid assets deposited by a Clearing Member must comprise at least what percentage of cash component?
e: At least 50% of liquid assets must be the cash component (cash, bank guarantees, FDR, T-bills, dated G-secs). The remainder can be non-cash (approved demat securities).

q: If a futures contract is not traded during the last 30 minutes on a day, the daily settlement price is computed as:
o: Theoretical price using F = S × e^(r×t)
Average of bid and ask at close
e: If untraded in the last 30 minutes, theoretical settlement = S × e^(r × t), where r is typically MIBOR or another specified rate.

q: On expiry day, all in-the-money index options are:
o: Held over to the next month
e: On expiry, all ITM options are deemed exercised by the clearing corporation (cash settled at the difference between strike and closing spot). OTM options expire worthless.
